# sizekit

> sizekit is a free browser toolkit for images and video. Resize one photo into 18 social and app
> presets with smart crop, compress images to a target size, convert between JPEG, PNG, WebP and
> AVIF, re-encode video with WebCodecs, build animated GIFs, make memes, and generate a complete
> favicon kit. Every file is processed on the visitor's own device — nothing is uploaded, there is
> no account, no watermark and no file limit.

Canonical: https://sizekit.vercel.app
Author: Rahul Sain — https://github.com/Anos714
Licence: free for personal and commercial use, no attribution required
Last updated: 2026-10-30

## What makes it different

- **Local processing.** Images are decoded by the browser's image decoder and re-encoded with its
  encoder. Video is decoded and encoded with WebCodecs on the local GPU and muxed into an MP4 in
  memory (`mp4-muxer`). No tool has an upload endpoint.
- **No server, no bill.** That is why every tool can be free with no quota.
- **Honest formats.** sizekit probes the browser's encoder at load and only offers a format the
  browser can actually produce, so a WebP is never a PNG in disguise.
- **Works offline.** After the page loads, no tool calls the network.

## Tools

### Resize (`/#tools`)
Batch-resize photos into 18 presets across Instagram (post, portrait, story), X, LinkedIn, Open
Graph, YouTube and app icons. Uses a saliency attention map — fine edges, coarse edges, saturation
and skin probability — plus a border penalty so faces are never sliced by a crop. Transparent
cut-outs are fitted, never cropped. A manual focal point can override the automatic crop. Results
download individually or as a ZIP. A 12-megapixel photo becomes nine sizes in roughly 440 ms.

### Compress (`/#tools`)
Reduce image weight with a live before/after total, a quality slider, an optional maximum edge and
an optional target size in kilobytes (encoder quality is binary-searched to fit). Converts to
JPEG, PNG, WebP or AVIF.

### Convert (`/#tools`)
Batch-convert JPEG, PNG, WebP and AVIF. Alpha is preserved where the target format supports it;
JPEG output is composited on white.

### Video (`/#tools`)
Compress MP4 and MOV in the browser with WebCodecs. The visitor chooses quality (bitrate budget),
resolution cap (source, 1080p, 720p, 480p) and whether to keep audio. Audio is re-encoded to AAC.
No ffmpeg.wasm, no upload, no server.

### GIF (`/#tools`)
Turn a sequence of stills into a looping GIF with a per-frame delay, width cap and palette size
(64, 128 or 256 colours). Frames can be reordered.

### Meme (`/#tools`)
100 built-in templates shipped with the app, or drop your own photo. Up to six captions, each
independently draggable with its own font, case, fill, outline and auto-fit size; the renderer is
shared by the preview and the full-resolution export. Search and tag filters find a template fast.
Exports PNG or JPG, or copies straight to the clipboard. Template images are credited to Imgflip
and their owners; rights stay with them.

### Favicon (`/#tools`)
Drop a square logo and get `favicon.ico` (16/32/48), `apple-touch-icon.png`, PNG icons for Android,
a `manifest.webmanifest` and the `<head>` snippet to paste.

## Common questions

**Does sizekit upload my files?** No. There is no upload endpoint. The Network panel shows no file
leaving the tab.

**Is it free?** Yes. No account, no trial, no watermark, no daily quota.

**Which browsers?** Any modern browser for the image tools. Video compression needs WebCodecs:
Chrome and Edge 94+, Safari 16.4+. Firefox support is partial.

**Can I use the output commercially?** Yes, with no attribution.

**Does it set cookies?** No cookies, no localStorage, no analytics.
